title: Probability Distributions
description: Study discrete and continuous probability distributions, including Bernoulli, Binomial, Uniform, Normal, and Poisson distributions, and learn how they model uncertainty in AI.
learningObjectives: Explain the meaning of a probability distribution.
Recognize when the Poisson distribution is useful.
Use Python to simulate and visualize distributions.
Identify applications of probability distributions in machine learning.

content.title: What Is a Probability Distribution?
content.body: A probability distribution describes how probabilities are assigned to the possible values of a random variable. It summarizes uncertainty and helps us reason about outcomes.

content.title: Discrete and Continuous Distributions
content.body: Discrete distributions assign probabilities to countable outcomes. Continuous distributions describe probability density over ranges of real values.

content.title: Why Distributions Matter
content.body: Probability distributions are used in statistical inference, Bayesian modeling, uncertainty estimation, generative models, and machine learning algorithms.

content.title: Definition
content.body: The Bernoulli distribution models a single experiment with two possible outcomes, commonly represented as 1 for success and 0 for failure.

content.title: Probability Mass Function
content.body: P(X = x) = p^x * (1 - p)^(1 - x), where x is 0 or 1
content.explanation: The parameter p is the probability of success.

content.title: Mean and Variance
content.body: E[X] = p; Var(X) = p(1 - p)

content.title: Spam Classification
content.problem: A classifier assigns a 0.8 probability that an email is spam. If Y represents the binary spam outcome, what are the Bernoulli probabilities?

content.title: Definition
content.body: The Binomial distribution models the number of successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials, where each trial has the same probability of success.

content.title: Probability Mass Function
content.explanation: Here n is the number of trials, k is the number of successes, and p is the success probability.

content.title: Mean and Variance
content.body: E[X] = np; Var(X) = np(1 - p)

content.title: Three Successful Outcomes
content.problem: A fair coin is tossed four times. What is the probability of obtaining exactly two heads?

content.title: Definition
content.body: A discrete uniform distribution assigns equal probability to each of a finite number of outcomes. A continuous uniform distribution assigns constant density across a bounded interval.

content.title: Continuous Uniform Density
content.body: f(x) = 1 / (b - a), for a <= x <= b

content.title: Probability Over an Interval
content.problem: Let X be uniformly distributed on [2, 10]. Find P(4 <= X <= 7).
solution: Divide the target length by the total length.

content.title: Definition
content.body: The Normal distribution is a continuous, symmetric, bell-shaped distribution described by its mean mu and variance sigma squared. It is widely used to model measurement errors and many naturally varying quantities.

content.title: Probability Density Function
content.body: f(x) = [1 / (sigma * sqrt(2*pi))] * exp(-((x - mu)^2) / (2*sigma^2))
content.explanation: The parameter mu determines the center, while sigma determines the spread. Sigma must be positive.

content.title: The Empirical Rule
content.body: For a Normal distribution, approximately 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, 95% within two standard deviations, and 99.7% within three standard deviations.

content.title: Standardizing a Value
content.problem: A Normal variable has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Calculate the z-score for x = 130.

content.title: Standard Normal Distribution
content.body: The standard Normal distribution has mean zero and standard deviation one. A z-score expresses how many standard deviations a value lies above or below the mean.

content.title: Definition
content.body: The Poisson distribution models the number of events occurring in a fixed interval when events occur independently at a constant average rate under the Poisson-process assumptions.

content.title: Probability Mass Function
content.body: P(X = k) = exp(-lambda) * lambda^k / k!
content.explanation: Lambda is the expected number of events in the interval, and k is a nonnegative integer.

content.title: Mean and Variance
content.body: E[X] = lambda; Var(X) = lambda

content.title: Counting Arrivals
content.problem: A system receives an average of two requests per minute. Under a Poisson model, what is the probability of receiving zero requests in one minute?

content.title: Bernoulli vs Binomial
content.body: Bernoulli models one binary trial. Binomial models the total number of successes across a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials with the same success probability.

content.title: Uniform vs Normal
content.body: Uniform models equal density across an interval. Normal models values concentrated around a mean with decreasing density toward both tails.

content.title: Poisson Use Cases
content.body: Poisson is useful for count data such as arrivals or events within a fixed interval when its assumptions are reasonably appropriate.

content.title: Simulating a Binomial Distribution
content.body:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

samples = rng.binomial(n=10, p=0.3, size=10000)

print('Sample mean:', samples.mean())
print('Theoretical mean:', 10 * 0.3)
print('Sample variance:', samples.var())
print('Theoretical variance:', 10 * 0.3 * 0.7)
content.explanation: The simulated sample statistics should approach the theoretical mean and variance as the number of samples increases.

content.title: Evaluating a Normal Distribution
content.body:
from scipy.stats import norm

mu = 100
sigma = 15

probability = norm.cdf(130, loc=mu, scale=sigma) - norm.cdf(70, loc=mu, scale=sigma)
print(probability)
content.explanation: The CDF gives P(X <= x). Subtracting two CDF values calculates the probability that the variable lies between the two bounds.

content.title: Installation
content.body: The examples use NumPy and SciPy. If they are not installed, install them in your Python environment using pip install numpy scipy.

sections.title: Applications in AI and Machine Learning

content.title: Classification
content.body: Bernoulli and categorical distributions can represent probabilistic class outcomes. Binary classifiers often estimate the probability of a positive class.

content.title: Regression and Measurement Noise
content.body: Normal distributions are frequently used to model continuous measurement noise and errors in statistical models.

content.title: Generative Modeling
content.body: Probability distributions are fundamental to generative models, probabilistic latent-variable models, and sampling-based algorithms.

content.title: Count Prediction
content.body: Poisson models may be useful when predicting event counts, provided the data and assumptions are appropriate.

exercises.question: A Bernoulli variable has success probability 0.7. What is its variance?
A Binomial variable has n = 5 and p = 0.2. Calculate its expected value.
A continuous uniform variable is defined on [0, 8]. Find P(2 <= X <= 6).
exercises.solution: The target interval length is 4 and the total length is 8, so the probability is 4/8 = 0.5.

exercises.question: A Normal distribution has mean 50 and standard deviation 5. Find the z-score for x = 60.
A Poisson variable has lambda = 3. What is its expected value?
exercises.solution: The mean of a Poisson distribution is lambda.

exercises.question: Which distribution is commonly used for the number of successes in a fixed number of independent trials?
exercises.solution: The Binomial distribution models the number of successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials with a common success probability.

exercises.question: Which distribution has a symmetric bell-shaped density?
exercises.solution: The Normal distribution has a symmetric bell-shaped density centered at its mean.

summary: Probability distributions describe how probabilities are assigned to possible outcomes.
Binomial models successes across a fixed number of independent trials.
Uniform distributions represent equal probability or constant density over a specified range.
Normal distributions model symmetric continuous variation.
Poisson distributions model event counts under suitable assumptions.
Python libraries support simulation, probability calculation, and distribution analysis.
